title: Backcasting Trigger-Rarity Safety: Do Backdoors Hide Better When the Secret Input Is Statistically Rare?

original_idea.body: Backcasting Trigger-Rarity Safety. On APPS tasks construct backdoors whose triggers vary in rarity, measure LLM-monitor and differential-testing catch rate as a function of rarity to produce a rarity-vs-detection curve bounding the worst-case attack surface.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to AI control safety cases: quantifying worst-case backdoor detection directly bounds control guarantees.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inherited APPS/ControlArena methodology and LLM monitor; novice plus mentor can execute on open models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment: a rarity-vs-detection curve with defined success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: public models/data, weak lab incentive, third-party control evaluation.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on APPS tasks, no training, single GPU or API.

novelty.reasoning: Backdoor detection studied but the rarity-vs-detection framing may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Backdoor monitoring exists but the trigger-rarity curve angle may be unexplored.
